available_assertion.statement: The actual D210 quaternionic surface has potentially good reduction everywhere, and E=L(A[11]) is Galois over Q with [E:Q]<2^66; A has good reduction over E at every residue characteristic different from11.
available_assertion.objects: The actual A/L with rational quaternion division action and all geometric Hom over the normal fiber field L, its full11-torsion field E and the semistable special-fiber torus.
available_assertion.hypotheses: The D210 normalizer and same-L Hom construction are supplied. The published semistable reduction and full-torsion criteria, Neron extension property and torus structure are retained. The normalizer maps can be scaled prime to11 using the split maximal order at11.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every place of A, and every conjugate of the full torsion field E; the good-reduction conclusion over E is for residue characteristics other than11.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Dimension two, division quaternion algebra B of discriminant210, degree[L:Q]≤576 and auxiliary prime11.
available_assertion.uniformity: The same Galois field E suffices simultaneously at2,3,5,7; no unbounded new extension is used for the later degree estimate.
available_assertion.normalizations: A positive torus rank t≤2 would give an injective unital B→M_t(Q), impossible for t=1 by dimension and for t=2 by division versus split algebra. Prime-to11 isogenies identify conjugate11-torsion kernels over L.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: The full-torsion reduction criterion is not applied at residue characteristic11. Potential good reduction alone does not imply the explicit field E is Galois; that uses normalizer maps prime to11.
available_assertion.limit_order: Pass temporarily to semistable reduction and exclude torus rank; construct prime-to11 conjugate isogenies over L; prove E is Galois and bound its degree; apply the full11-torsion criterion and torus argument.

available_assertion.statement: For an abelian variety over a characteristic-zero field, rational matrix units give abelian image factors over that same field, mutually isogenous via off-diagonal units; complementary images sum by an isogeny.
available_assertion.objects: The original A/L with its L-defined M2(k) action, diagonal idempotents e11,e22 and a common positive integer denominator m.
available_assertion.hypotheses: The idempotents and matrix units belong to End_L^0(A); the image construction uses properness, geometric connectedness, and smoothness of finite-type group schemes in characteristic zero (the retained Cartier input).
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every rational matrix-unit system on this same abelian variety and every common denominator clearing it.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero; here dim A=2 and the two matrix-unit factors have equal positive dimension.
available_assertion.uniformity: All images and maps are defined over L; no further field extension is introduced.
available_assertion.constants: Choose any positive integer m clearing the matrix-unit denominators; no uniform isogeny-degree bound is asserted by this algebraic construction.
available_assertion.normalizations: X_i=image(m e_ii); addition p and tuple q satisfy pq=[m] and qp=[m]. Off-diagonal units provide rational isomorphisms between X_i, and End^0(X_i)=e_ii End^0(A)e_ii.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Images do not depend on the chosen denominator. This is not a polarization-preserving isogeny assertion and does not give a good-reduction field bound or a quantitative isogeny estimate.
available_assertion.limit_order: First obtain L-defined full endomorphisms; then clear denominators, construct the images, and use the matrix-unit identities. Dimension two gives elliptic factors; the corner k gives CM.

needed_assertion.quantifiers: Every selected prime in each such pattern, after the fixed bad primes are excluded.
needed_assertion.parameter_range: N tends to infinity with the finite pattern and curve fixed; q=p_j at this split residue place.
needed_assertion.uniformity: The Hasse constant2 is absolute; the O(sqrt(N)) comparison is uniform in the fixed finite list of forms.
needed_assertion.constants: Exact bound2sqrt(p_j), with central value p_j+1.
needed_assertion.normalizations: d_+ counts all F_{p_j}-points including infinity. It is not a count over F_{p_j^2}.

needed_assertion.limit_order: Fix curve/forms and exclude bad primes, obtain patterns in the specified range, then apply Hasse. Use gap and divisibility arguments separately to exclude selected-prime divisors of opposite group orders.

available_assertion.statement: For a bounded finite free complex over a DVR, equality of generic and residue cohomology dimensions in every degree implies free cohomology commuting with reduction; its actual class-functional determinant tensor specializes in the same retained basis.
available_assertion.objects: A bounded finite free DVR complex C, actual cycle, actual closed functional and retained determinant basis.
available_assertion.hypotheses: Generic and residue cohomology dimensions agree in every degree. For the stated tensor coordinate the only nonzero dimensions are (1,1) in degrees one and two.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every such bounded complex and actual cycle-functional pair.
available_assertion.parameter_range: A discrete valuation ring A with uniformizer t, fraction field F and residue field k.
available_assertion.uniformity: An exact algebraic implication; no uniform quantitative bound is inferred.
available_assertion.constants: No new numeric constant; only unit determinants from contractible summands occur.
available_assertion.normalizations: Use det inverse C and retain its same contractible-summand identifications before and after reduction.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Dimension equality cannot be omitted. A positive-valuation two-term disk raises residue dimensions in two adjacent degrees and is excluded by the hypothesis.
available_assertion.limit_order: Smith-reduce the bounded complex; exclude all positive-valuation disks using all-degree dimension equalities; remove only unit disks; specialize the actual tensor.

Central valuations and zeros transfer whenever the primitive coordinate is regular.
available_assertion.objects: Actual primitive-to-relaxed map i and paired strict map j, actual retained classes and their own closed functionals, unused-prime factors e_q=a_q-z-z^(-1), two-place quotient factor l_q, and finite binary groupG.
available_assertion.hypotheses: The retained norm identity and boundary, cup-pairing naturality and original integral determinant bases are supplied. Every graph prime, including unused ones, has the prescribed scalar exponent. Rational E[2] makes a_q even at good oddq.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Each unused good split prime and every character of the same finite binary family, with one eta before character evaluation.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Lambda=Z2[[t]], O its completed localization at(2); good oddq and common graph-wide moving character.
available_assertion.uniformity: The correction is constructed in the original O[G] for the whole family, without character-by-character interpolation or group-order denominators.
available_assertion.constants: l_q*u_rel=e_q^2*epsilon_q*u_prim; q^2*l_q=e_q^2+(q-1)(q-1-(z+z^(-1))*e_q); v_q=(l_q/e_q^2-1)/2.
available_assertion.normalizations: Both the actual class and its own paired functional contribute onee_q. Comparison signs and unit disks give Lambda units, not merelyO units. eta is the product of1+v_q(1+g_q).
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: eta_x can have a pole at t=0; only its product withu_rel,x is specialized. No integral self-duality of the primitive condition or interpolation ofepsilon_x is assumed.
available_assertion.limit_order: Use the actual norm boundary and pairing naturality; compare quotient determinants in retained bases; prove e_q is anO[G]unit via reduction t^2/(1+t); construct integralv_q and oneeta; then evaluate characters and transfer regular central data.

available_assertion.hypotheses: The parametrization is dominant over Q; its domain meets the input chart in a nonempty open; X1/X0 is nonconstant.
available_assertion.quantifiers: For the exact current objects and each place or point quantified in the indicated argument.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero over Q; the actual cubic dimension>=2 branch where applicable.
available_assertion.uniformity: No quantitative parametrization or new uniformity assertion is introduced.
available_assertion.constants: No numerical constant is required.
available_assertion.normalizations: Shrink to a rational affine principal open avoiding the denominator. No density of rational points on the cubic itself is assumed.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Lower-dimensional branches and positive characteristic are outside this use.
available_assertion.limit_order: Dominance preserves nonconstancy in function fields. Choose a real ball in the affine principal open. Rational density and continuity put its whole image in the closed set Z; connectedness makes that image constant. The numerator minus this constant times the denominator vanishes on a real open ball, hence identically, contradiction.

needed_assertion.statement: The actual sections J^2 q_i, already regular at every codimension-one point, extend uniquely across codimension two on the maximal stack.
needed_assertion.objects: The regular Noetherian maximal D210 Deligne-Mumford stack and its invertible square-dualizing line with rational sections J^2 q0,J^2 q1.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: The stack is regular and flat over the base. The line is invertible, the sections are regular on the generic fibre, and the separately proved vertical valuation bounds give regularity at vertical codimension-one points.
needed_assertion.quantifiers: Both displayed sections, on every regular etale chart and every codimension-one point.
needed_assertion.parameter_range: The actual maximal stack, including primes dividing210; no tame coarse quotient is assumed there.
needed_assertion.uniformity: The same rational sections and line extend; no rescaling beyond the already fixed J^2.
needed_assertion.constants: J remains2765952000; no new height constant.
needed_assertion.normalizations: Trivialize the line on affine regular etale charts; apply the source with M=R, a free rank-one and hence reflexive module.
needed_assertion.exceptional_cases: This does not construct a coarse-model line bundle, supply the valuation bounds, or extend a general nonreflexive sheaf.
needed_assertion.limit_order: Choose an etale scheme atlas of the regular Noetherian Deligne-Mumford maximal stack and trivialize the invertible square-dualizing line on affine open charts. Each connected regular chart is a normal domain. The generic bicanonical section is regular at horizontal height-one primes; the separate vertical valuation calculation proves it at vertical height-one primes. Apply Tag0AVB with the free rank-one module, which is reflexive, to obtain a unique regular section on each chart. The extensions agree on etale overlaps because they agree on the dense generic fibre and the line is locally free on a reduced flat atlas. Descent for sections gives the unique section on the stack. No coarse-model pullback or tame argument at bad primes is used.
